item.title: Week 40 — Users, incident relations and service logic
item.description:
Weekly summary

This week I extended CIT from storing individual incidents to connecting them to users. I also introduced DAO interfaces, prepared an isolated database test setup and added an incident service for validation and application operations. This summary covers the work available through 3 October; the week is still in progress.

What I implemented

  • Added a User entity with an automatically generated ID, a required name and a required, unique email address.
  • Linked each incident to a reporter through a required, unidirectional ManyToOne relationship. Several incidents can refer to the same user through reported_by_id.
  • Added UserDAO methods for creating users and finding a user by email. Added a parameterised JPQL query in IncidentDAO to find incidents by reporter ID, ordered by incident ID.
  • Introduced IUserDAO and IIncidentDAO to describe the available persistence operations. Incident CRUD remains in the DAO layer, with transactions and rollback for writes.
  • Updated the manual example in Main to connect an incident to a stored user, retrieve it and list incidents belonging to that reporter.
  • Added IncidentService, which depends on the DAO interfaces. It supports creating incidents, finding one or all incidents, listing by reporter, changing status and deleting incidents.

The service rejects blank titles and reporter emails, missing severity, descriptions longer than 2,000 characters, invalid IDs and null status values. It looks up an existing reporter before creation and throws an exception when a required user or incident cannot be found. New incidents retain the entity’s default OPEN status.

item.title: Week 38 — Building the incident data layer
item.description:
Weekly summary

This week I established the persistence foundation of the backend. The recorded implementation work is from 18–19 September.

What I implemented

I worked on the foundation of SM3-CIT, my Cyber Incident Tracker project, using Java, JPA/Hibernate and PostgreSQL.

  • Set up the project packages and an Incident entity with an ID, title and description.
  • Implemented an IncidentDAO to create, find, list, update and delete incidents.
  • Used database transactions with commit and rollback for operations that change data.
  • Added a small program in Main to manually try out the CRUD flow using a test incident.

I confirmed that the CRUD flow worked before moving on to status and severity. This was a manual check, rather than an automated test suite.

item.title: SM3-CIT
item.description:
Cyber Incident Tracker

SM3-CIT is my third-semester Cyber Incident Tracker project. I am building the backend in Java, using JPA/Hibernate and PostgreSQL. This portfolio documents the implementation and its connection to the course through the backend exam in early November 2026.

Current implementation

As of 3 October, the project contains incident CRUD, status and severity enums, users and a required relationship between incidents and their reporters. DAO interfaces define persistence operations, and JPQL supports finding users by email and incidents by reporter. An incident service adds validation and application operations on top of the DAOs.
